oewn-02543752-v.learner: to make a social or emotional tie between people.
examples: Lydia had wanted only encouragement to attach herself to anybody.

oewn-01299048-v.learner: to make one thing be joined or fixed to another.
examples: She attached a label to each of the trunks.

oewn-01292858-v.learner: to be joined or fixed to something, or to be touching it.
examples: The wife of Mr. Darcy must have such extraordinary sources of happiness necessarily attached to her situation.

oewn-07536913-n.learner: a feeling of fear about something you think is coming.
examples: all her apprehension of meeting its owner returned
the boys were relieved from their apprehension of Charlotte's dying an old maid

oewn-05960433-n.learner: the painful feeling of expecting something.
examples: With the kindest concern he came on to Longbourn, and broke his apprehensions to us.

oewn-00089545-n.learner: the act of catching and holding someone, especially a criminal.
examples: The apprehension of the thief took the officers only a few hours.

oewn-07518219-n.learner: a feeling that someone or something deserves no respect, together with strong dislike.
examples: Elizabeth was convinced that they held her in contempt for it
cheating a person of their premeditated contempt

oewn-06728866-n.learner: disrespect for a person or thing that is shown openly.
examples: the contempt shown to the rest of her family
you can treat the mention of his misfortunes with contempt and ridicule

oewn-04922864-n.learner: a way of behaving that shows no respect for people.
examples: The expression of his face changed gradually from indignant contempt to a composed and steady gravity.

connotation.why: names a person's whole manner as showing no respect

oewn-00973682-v.learner: to state your judgment about someone or something.
examples: they admired her and liked her, and pronounced her to be a sweet girl
The Bennets were speedily pronounced to be the luckiest family in the world

oewn-00980581-v.learner: to speak or say a word or sound in a certain way.
examples: As she pronounced these words, Mr. Darcy changed colour.

oewn-02553283-v.learner: to give help to someone, or to be of use to them.
examples: We are persuaded that he has pledged himself to assist Mr. Wickham with money.
there are still some who are able and willing to assist him in the army

oewn-02419840-v.learner: to work under someone else, doing a supporting part of their job.
examples: He assists the head gardener three days a week.

oewn-02546367-v.learner: to work for someone, or to be their servant.
examples: A young footman assisted the family at table for many years.

oewn-00914001-v.learner: to say something out loud, often out of surprise, horror, or joy.
examples: "To Jane herself," she exclaimed, "there could be no possibility of objection"
She wished to discredit it entirely, repeatedly exclaiming, "This must be false!"

oewn-00979368-v.learner: to state something, or to announce it.
examples: He exclaimed his refusal so that the whole hall knew it.

oewn-00597981-s.learner: going on without a break and continuing for a long time with no end in sight.
examples: no excellence in music is to be acquired without constant practice
It was the prospect of constant society, and good society.
The oven holds a constant heat all through the baking.

oewn-00585590-a.learner: firm and unchanging in what you aim at, or in your devotion, or in your love.
examples: She was constant in her affection for him through every trouble.

connotation.why: praises a person for holding firm

oewn-02638248-v.learner: to have something as a quality, a piece of knowledge, or a skill.
examples: it is happy for you that you possess the talent of flattering with delicacy
I certainly have not the talent which some people possess of conversing easily with those I have never seen before

oewn-02209474-v.learner: to own something, or to have it as yours.
examples: He possesses a small house and a piece of land near the river.

oewn-02653395-v.learner: to get inside a person and take control of them, as a feeling or an idea can.
examples: A sudden fear possessed her, and she could not speak.

oewn-07507795-n.learner: the comfort you feel when someone eases your disappointment.
examples: it will then be but poor consolation to believe the world equally in the dark
"An excellent consolation in its way," said Elizabeth

oewn-01214157-n.learner: the act of comforting someone, giving relief to a person in trouble.
examples: anything could be either said or done on my part, that might offer consolation to such distress
pour into the wounded bosoms of each other the balm of sisterly consolation

oewn-06638793-n.learner: a short letter written to a person you know.
examples: the entrance of the footman with a note for Miss Bennet; it came from Netherfield
she requested to have a note sent to Longbourn

oewn-06516453-n.learner: a few words written down to keep a record of something.
examples: He kept notes of every lesson in a small book.

oewn-06878395-n.learner: a written sign that shows how high a musical sound is and how long it lasts.
examples: She could not yet read the notes on the page.
